rule: Never edited. tools/final_completion.py --check fails if any of these IDs disappears or changes meaning.

requirements.text: A tenant's data is reachable only through that tenant's database login and row-level security
Legal entities, regions and business units are master data with roll-ups
Group → entity → book/branch hierarchy with effective-dated joint-venture and intercompany relationships
A project moves through phases only by an approved stage gate (maker/checker, fresh MFA)
Portfolio roll-up across projects and entities with FX as-of rates (no naive sum of currencies)
Programs group projects with a dependency graph and investment gates
Rule-based risk assessments are recorded as snapshots with their inputs
OKRs, decision log and risk register with owners and due dates
Every dashboard tile equals the report it drills into; the KPI catalogue documents formula and source
13-week cash projection separating certified, billed and collected amounts
Daily exception digest by e-mail or Telegram
Lead and opportunity pipeline
Feasibility and discounted cash-flow scenarios with documented assumptions
Land and permit records
Tender calendar, confidential bid room, eligibility checklist, bid approval and submission record
BOQ versions are approved by a second person; the approved version supersedes the previous one and is never overwritten
Spreadsheet import is staged, reviewed and committed explicitly, with row errors reported
PDF and IFC take-off arrive as reviewed suggestions, never as authoritative quantities
Rate build-up: resources × rates + overhead, contingency and escalation; selling rate = full cost / (1 − margin); markup kept distinct
Every rate carries source, region, currency, FX date, validity and approval; rates freeze at bid submission
Bid scenarios and comparison of estimate against actual historical rates
Original, revised and current budget; revisions and transfers need a second person and cannot overspend under concurrency
Available budget is checked when a commitment is approved; consumed commitments are not counted twice
CPM with FS/SS/FF/SF links, lags and calendars; cycles and invalid networks are refused
Approved baselines, progress at a status date and earned value; undefined ratios are null, not zero
Monte Carlo delay forecast (P50/P80) with reproducible seeds and stated distributions
Look-ahead and Last Planner constraint tracking
Resource- and cost-loaded schedules; levelling proposals never alter an approved schedule silently
Project risk register with quantified exposure feeding contingency
Work packages released only with approved drawings, permits, ITP, resources and predecessor acceptance
Daily site diaries (labour, equipment, notes) are versioned, approved by a project manager and corrected, never overwritten
Photographs, weather, delays and instructions on the daily report
Measurements are prepared by one person and verified by another; certified quantity cannot be counted twice
Measurement book lines carry method, chainage/location, drawing revision, dimensions and evidence
Progress reports against the approved baseline are approved before they count
Installed, measured, certified, billed and collected quantities are reported side by side
Engineering deliverables register linked to RFIs and submittals
IFC import in an isolated parser; object identity by model revision + GlobalId; mapping to BOQ/WBS
Installed-asset records with measured/estimated/reported/certified data classes
PostGIS spatial objects with explicit coordinate reference system and chainage
Reorder rules flag items below their level
Material demand generated from schedule and BOQ, netted against stock
Requisition → RFQ → award → purchase order → goods receipt → three-way match → payment, reconciled to the ledger
No self-approval, no split-order bypass; authority limits apply to purchase orders
Receipt and matching tolerances; duplicate supplier invoices are refused
Supplier bank details are dual-controlled, masked, encrypted at rest and revealed only with MFA and a purpose
Supplier-level exposure triggers dual payment approval
Supplier qualification, conflict disclosure and performance scoring
Subcontracts: scope/BOQ, security, measured work, retention, deductions
Stock quantity and value move together (FIFO or weighted average) and reconcile to the inventory account
Stock cannot go negative, including by raw SQL and under concurrent movements
Reservations reduce what can be issued
Returns, scrap and quarantine
Transfers between warehouses pass through in-transit and leave no value residue
Bins, lots/batches and serial numbers
Delivery tracking, haulage and inland logistics
Import file: pro forma, LC, customs, freight and landed-cost allocation by a documented basis
Unit conversions are approved data; incompatible conversions are refused
BOQ theoretical quantity against actual issues and installation (waste)
Asset register, assignment, utilisation and monotonic meter readings
A fourteen-state lifecycle enforced identically in Go and in the database; every move is an attested human decision with a reason; history is written by the database and cannot be edited
Equipment on safety hold, broken down, under maintenance or under inspection cannot be put to work or reserved, and returns to service only through a certifier with fresh MFA
Approved reservations of one machine never overlap, also under concurrent approval; a machine reaches a project only through that project's approved reservation
Daily logs: one per machine, day and shift; an authorised operator; hours fit the meter and the day; the machine is at the project; approved by a second person; an offline repeat is recorded once
A meter never runs backwards and moves only through an approved log or an approved, two-person meter reset; replacement and rollover are recorded
Fleet data is invisible to other tenants; project hours are visible only inside the project scope; the register pages by cursor
Fleet Command Centre figures (counts by state, hours, utilization, availability, fuel per hour) equal the register and the approved logs; a ratio with no data is absent, not zero
Work-package assignment, capacity planning, cross-project requests, availability forecasting, rental agreements, standby periods
Attachments, equipment documents and photographs, fixed-asset linkage, warranty and insurance expiry alerts
Daily logs captured offline through the field device command log
Telematics ingestion (GPS, engine hours, fuel level) with authenticated devices and replay protection, stored apart from accounting data
Deterministic allocation and transfer recommendations with explainable constraints

Equipment costing and charge-out: operating cost per machine (fuel, parts, labour, workshop), internal charge-out and rental to projects as a management allocation kept apart from statutory postings, idle-time and utilisation rules, external rental, equipment profitability; rates and rules as approved, effective-dated policy
Fuel issues linked to asset, operator, meter and stock movement; variance review

Fuel is ordinary stock: a dispense is a stock issue of a designated fuel item, prepared with the machine, meter reading and operator, and takes effect (tank quantity, value, journal, project cost) only when a second person approves the issue; there is no second fuel ledger

A dispense is refused for an item not designated as fuel, a machine not at the project, a meter reading behind the last approved one, or more than the tank holds; an offline retry records once; a tenant database login cannot write or alter a dispense around the kernel
Fuel items and fuel standards (litres per metered unit, effective-dated, append-only) are set only by a person with fleet.approve, attested

Per machine and period, dispensed, logged and expected fuel are compared and differences beyond a stated threshold are listed with both figures, in the API and the console, limited to the reader's projects
Recorded investigation and approved closure of a fuel variance; tank dip readings reconciled to the stock ledger; fuel sensors (telematics)

The thresholds for listing a fuel difference and for a service being due soon are an approved, versioned, effective-dated fleet policy (prepared by fleet.manage, approved by another person with fleet.approve and a fresh second factor); reports name the policy applied, and say so when only engineering defaults exist

Expected fuel for a period that spans several effective-dated standards is the sum of each approved log's metered units at the standard in force on that log's date; days logged with no standard in force predict nothing and are reported
Maintenance plans, work orders, parts and downtime

A work order is prepared (plant staff; site staff for a breakdown of a machine at their project), authorised by fleet.approve with a fresh second factor, reported complete by plant staff and closed or sent back by a certifier who did not report it; a decided work order never changes; none of these decisions can be taken by an AI or service principal

A machine that has been under maintenance returns to service only after a work order for it was closed after it entered maintenance, never while a work order is open, and not by passing through inspection; an earlier work order does not release a later spell

A part used on a work order is an ordinary stock issue linked to the work order: approved by a second person, valued by the stock ledger, charged to the machine's project; a work order is not reported complete while a part awaits approval
Preventive plans by metered units and/or days show what is due; a plan is raised as one work order at a time and moves on only when a certifier closes that work order

Maintenance history per machine (work orders, labour hours, parts cost from the stock ledger) and hours out of service by state from the lifecycle history; a tenant database login cannot write work orders, parts or plans around the kernel
Labour cost of maintenance, workshop cost centres for machines not at a project, parts reservation per work order, retiring or changing a plan, safety inspection checklists

Separation on a work order as enforced in the kernel and in the database: the authoriser is not the preparer; the certifier is none of the preparer, the authoriser or the reporter; authorising and certifying each need a fresh second factor at the database boundary; an attestation serves one decision on one record once; forged session settings and direct writes are refused; other projects and tenants reach nothing

A preventive plan is revised by a new version that retires the old one in the same transaction and continues from its last service, or retired with a reason; retired plans are kept, are not due and take no work orders; neither is possible while a work order of the plan is open
Capitalisation, depreciation and disposal posted through the ledger
Employee and contractor records with protected personal data
Attendance and timesheets with approval, duplicate and overlap detection
Payroll preview → approval → locked run → posting → payment, on effective-dated reviewed rules
Crew output and labour cost by work package
Certifications and safety training with expiry
Contracts with approved lines, advance, retention and policy; the signed version is never overwritten
Guarantees register, liquidated-damages terms and contract obligations
Variations are approved by a second person before they change contract value; pending and approved stay separate
Change events carry cost impact into a draft budget revision
Notices with a computed time bar; claims prepared and approved by different people; the client's answer recorded once
Payment certificate = cumulative certified − previous, less retention and advance recovery; never negative; no duplicate certification
Retention release, credit notes and price adjustment are separate approved documents
Certification, invoice, revenue recognition and collection are distinct states
A journal posts only if balanced, in an open period, with valid accounts; enforced in Go and in the database
Posted journals are immutable; correction is by reversal
The same source posts once: replay returns the original, a changed payload conflicts
Posting and period close cannot race
Balance sheet, income statement and cash-flow statement
Supplier invoices post through bound draft journals; payables reconcile to the control account
Customer invoices, receipts and credit notes reconcile to the receivable control account, including under concurrency
Cost codes are validated against the approved WBS
Monthly cost forecast (EAC/ETC), WIP schedule and budget-vs-actual tie to their sources
Payments are prepared, approved and released by different people and settled only by an independent bank statement
FX rates are policy-bound, maker/checker approved and re-checked at posting
Bank transfers through a bank API
Tax rules are effective-dated data with review status; ambiguity is an error
Real jurisdiction tax and withholding rules
Intercompany matching, translation and elimination for consolidated statements
Cash forecast scenarios including payroll, tax and supplier schedules
Every command writes a hash-chained audit entry and its outbox event in the same transaction
A tenant login cannot rewrite history
Audit chain anchored to separately protected storage
ITP with hold/witness points, NCR and corrective action through independent closure
Samples with chain of custody, calibrated equipment, results against limits; failed tests preserved
Permits to work, incidents, toolbox talks; stop-work effective offline; no AI release
Carbon, waste, water and energy records with versioned factors; measured vs estimated
A controlled document has immutable revisions; content is hashed by the database; a revision is published by a second person with fresh MFA
Publishing a revision supersedes the previous one in the same transaction; there is never more than one current revision
Documents are visible only inside the tenant and the reader's project scope; every download is recorded
Malware scanning and quarantine before a file can be downloaded
Object storage with pre-signed, short-lived URLs and resumable upload
Transmittals, QR verification of a revision, retention policy and legal hold
Files over the PostgreSQL cap are stored encrypted in an S3-compatible store under a tenant-scoped, immutable key fixed by the database; a tampered, swapped or cross-tenant object is not served
Migration from PostgreSQL to object storage is incremental and repeatable, verifies each copy by reading it back, and removes no byte until the schema owner releases it
Download links are short-lived, bound to tenant, revision and person, re-checked against quarantine when used and audited; downloads and links count against the export budget
Uploads are streamed with bounded memory and refused when mislabelled, an archive bomb, a path traversal, SVG/HTML, or carrying macros or active PDF content; refusals are audited
The scan requirement and storage quota are a per-tenant policy changed only by a person with tenant.settings.manage and fresh MFA, attested
Safe document preview generation
Resumable multipart upload from the client for very large BIM and engineering files

Storage faults are told apart (missing bucket, missing object, refused credentials, unavailable service); the bucket is provisioned and proven private before use; the API refuses to start without it and never reports a storage fault as a missing file
Document encryption keys are versioned: rotation keeps earlier files readable, a missing key is reported as such and is recoverable, scan verdicts survive a rotation
Drawings are controlled documents: the current revision is the only one offered as current
Mark-ups and 2D review
An RFI is raised against a project (optionally a document revision), answered once by someone other than its author, then closed
RFI cost/time impact linked to change events
Submittals with review cycles and consultant responses
Correspondence register (in/out) linked to contracts
Versioned workflow definitions; thresholds, quorum, maker excluded; the database refuses a forged approval trail
An approval is bound to the exact document content, step and outcome, and cannot be replayed
Authority matrix and time-limited delegation that cannot defeat separation of duties
Alert rules notify the right people; a rule is activated by someone other than its author
Assignable tasks with due dates outside document approvals
Meeting minutes with actions and decisions
Every catalogued report runs and ties to its source; exports show no more than the screen and are budgeted
Client portal limited to the client's own contracts, certificates and documents
Supplier portal limited to the supplier's own RFQs, orders and invoices
Consultant portal for scoped review and certification
Government/regulator portal
Unit inventory, atomic reservation, sale agreements and instalments
Service requests, preventive maintenance, leases and utilities
Commissioning checks and final acceptance
Handover package: as-built revisions, manuals, warranties, punch list
Lessons learned and authorised document retrieval with ACL before search
An AI principal can draft but never approve, post, pay or release; enforced in Go and in the database
The assistant answers only from permission-filtered computed facts and shows sources
Model-independent gateway, agent registry and evaluation sets
A live model provider
Sessions can be revoked across replicas, including in-flight approvals
The approval signing key lives outside the API; a compromised API cannot forge an approval
Pre-authentication abuse limits shared across replicas
Production configuration fails closed on any demo default
Independent penetration test; a real identity provider with step-up; HSM/KMS custody of the signer key
Directory of people, custom roles and grants; identity administrators hold no financial permission
Tenant settings and a setup checklist that reads real state
Access reviews, legal hold and break-glass access
Offline commands are idempotent: a lost acknowledgement or a retry applies once; conflicts are returned, never merged
A revoked device is refused
Native field app with an encrypted local database, restart-safe queue and 7-day offline objective
Offline stock issue through expiring quantity rights; offline stop-work
Tenant routing with a dedicated-database tier
Partitioned high-volume tables with partition-independent source identity
Archive catalogue, verified export to open formats and reconciled restore
Measured load at tier T1 or above
Base backup plus WAL archive restores exactly to a named point, every migration included; data loss on losing the primary is measured
Encrypted, signed offsite PITR backup restores exactly; forged or colliding archives are refused
Request telemetry, trace context and alert rules fire on induced failures
Outbox relay delivers in order, retries, dead-letters and replays; consumers dedupe
Operated staging and production environments
Exact decimal money per ISO 4217 minor units; ETB supported
Ethiopic text renders in PDF exports
Ethiopian calendar display and input with round-trip tests
Translated interface (Amharic, Tigrinya, Afan Oromo)
Ethiopian statutory tax, payroll and forms
The OpenAPI contract matches the routes served
Problem details per RFC 9457 and cursor pagination on every list
